# BarChart

> A handful of figures side by side as bars, with a label under each: grey, and green for the one that matters now. For months, not for analysis.

## Install

It lands in `src/rost/bar-chart/`, with what it needs and its contract. In an app that uses shadcn:

```sh
npx shadcn add https://rost.build/r/bar-chart.json
```

Then import `src/rost/fonts.css` and `src/rost/tokens.css` once, at the root of the app. More on this in [Install](../INSTALL.md).

## Props

| Prop | Type | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data` | node |  |  |
| `current` | number |  |  |
| `max` | number |  |  |
| `height` | number |  | `160` |
| `label` | string |  |  |

## Anatomy

- `root`: An `<ol>`, one item per bar, side by side and sharing the width, 8px apart. Its height comes from the `height` prop.
- `item`: An `<li>`: the bar's room, then its label, 8px apart.
- `plot`: The room a full bar would take. The bar stands at its bottom.
- `bar`: A bar, as tall as its value out of `max`, in a field's edge grey, with 4px corners on top.
- `current-bar`: The bar for now: the same shape, in the primary green.
- `label`: Under each bar, centred, in label type and the tertiary grey.
- `current-label`: The label for now, medium weight in the main text colour.

## When to use

- **How this month compares.** Income for the last six months, with this one in green. The Stat above it says the number; the bars say whether it's up.

## When not to use

- **Many bars.** Past about twelve the labels don't fit and the bars blur. Use a **Table**.
- **Exact comparisons.** Bars without an axis show shape, not amounts. When the amounts matter, write them.

## Behaviour

Each bar's height is its value out of `max`, which is the largest value unless you set it. It has no axis, gridlines or tooltips, on purpose.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: `<ol>` with an `aria-label`, so it's read as a list of so many items. Each `<li>` says its label and value in words.
- **Name**: `label`: what the chart shows, like Income by month.
- **Colour**: The grey bars are 4.3:1 on the dark page and the green one 10:1. The current label is also heavier, so the colour isn't the only sign.

## Content

Short labels, like Jun or Q3. Give `valueText` in the units people read, like €1,200.
